title: How Small Can We Go? Calibrating Activation-Cache Compression for SAE Training
abstract: arXiv:2611.08551v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: To train a sparse autoencoder (SAE), you need a massive cache of model activations. We look into the effects that compression has on an SAE in two ways: we keep the original fp32-trained SAE and pass the compressed cache into the same SAE to see how many feature activations stay the same (the frozen-SAE test), and we retrain an SAE on the compressed cache and see how many of the original features still exist (the retraining test). We found that in the retraining test, there is no clear scale for retained features. On a GPT-2 cache, rounding everything to fp16 keeps 60.6% of features, but changing one value in a million by the smallest step fp32 allows (a change eight orders of magnitude smaller) keeps only 70.5%. Meanwhile, changing the random seed keeps 23.0%. For the frozen-SAE test, the frozen SAE's correlation with the original increases in order of how precise the codecs are, but plain $L_2$ distance gives nearly the same ordering

translated_title: 我们能压缩到多小？为SAE训练校准激活缓存压缩
translated_abstract: 训练稀疏自编码器（SAE）需要海量的模型激活缓存。我们通过两种方式研究压缩对SAE的影响：一是保留原始用fp32训练的SAE，将压缩后的缓存输入同一SAE，观察有多少特征激活保持不变（冻结SAE测试）；二是在压缩后的缓存上重新训练SAE，观察有多少原始特征仍然存在（重训练测试）。我们发现在重训练测试中，保留特征的比例没有清晰的规模规律。在GPT-2缓存上，将所有数值四舍五入为fp16保留了60.6%的特征，而仅改变百万分之一的数值且变化幅度为fp32允许的最小步长（比前者小八个数量级）只保留了70.5%的特征；相比之下，改变随机种子则保留了23.0%的特征。对于冻结SAE测试，冻结SAE与原始结果的相关性随编解码器精度的提高而递增，但简单的L2距离就能给出几乎相同的排序。
tldr: 该论文通过冻结SAE测试和重训练测试研究激活缓存压缩对稀疏自编码器训练的影响，发现特征保留比例缺乏清晰规律，且SAE训练对微小的数值扰动也异常敏感。
en_tdlr: The paper examines how activation-cache compression affects SAE training through frozen-SAE and retraining tests, revealing that retained feature proportions show no clear scaling pattern and that SAE training is surprisingly sensitive to even minute numerical perturbations.
